- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.36) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period if sentiment remains high.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows when sentiment is negative (especially <0.2) — add 3–7% to forecast if sentiment turns neutral or positive.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price drops — cap forecast increases at 3–5% above prior peak if sentiment is weak.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is 3–5% below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, adjust next forecast down by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- Sentiment-driven overshoot: if sentiment >0.4 and forecast >85%, reduce by 5–10% to avoid overbought bias.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in cycle (first 5–7 days) — apply 2–4% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or declining.
